description: Default search space for `mtgsim tune`: settings of Forge's heuristic AI (Monte Carlo off) that plausibly decide how control and value decks fare against creature decks. Each parameter lists alternative values to Default.ai's; a parameter with several keys changes them together. FLAT_MC_* settings that only act while Monte Carlo search is on are left out (Monte Carlo is a separate study), except the mulligan ones, which act in every game. Chosen after reading forge-ai's AiProps.java, the code that reads each key, and the built-in profiles (Cautious, Reckless and Experimental differ from Default mainly in these). Note that with Monte Carlo off no profile key makes the AI hold up mana for counterspells; that is FLAT_MC_CONSIDER_HOLDING / FLAT_MC_HOLD_MANA_WEIGHT.

params.name: counter-chances
params.why: Default counters a 1-drop 30% and a 2-drop 75% of the time (CounterAi). Saving counters for bigger threats (Cautious: 0/50/100) or countering everything changes how long a counterspell deck survives a curve of cheap creatures.
Below this mana value the AI only counters removal, burn, pump, auras and other counterspells (Cautious and Reckless use 2).

params.name: counter-tricks
params.why: Default spends counters on any pump spell, aura or burn spell regardless of the thresholds above; keeping them for threats is what human control players do.

params.name: danger-threshold
params.why: Life total below which the AI blocks and removes attackers to stay alive (ComputerUtilCombat.lifeInDanger, also read by several card AIs). Default 4 lets aggro decks race a control deck down to almost nothing; Hardest uses 6.

params.name: block-trades
params.why: Chance to block for an even trade (AiBlockController.wouldLikeToRandomlyTrade), rising as life falls. Control decks want to trade early; creature decks want to keep attackers.
Default only trades on blocks when it has at least as many creatures; a deck with few creatures (control) then never trades.
All-out attacking (AiAttackController). Default is off; it also changes how a deck Forge thinks is non-aggro (name contains Control, or average mana value above 3) holds back blockers.
Default 0 (the AiProps default is 40, Reckless 100): how often the AI attacks into a block that trades creatures. Aggro decks overperform in the simulator, so this works in both directions.
Whether attacks into trades are made into open mana (combat tricks, flash blockers, instant removal). Default 30, Cautious 0.
Default only attacks into trades while holding mana for a trick; Reckless also does when tapped out.
Extra checks that stop attacks which cannot deal damage (Cautious and Reckless turn them off).

params.name: hold-tricks
params.why: Casting pump spells after blocks rather than before; mostly affects creature decks.
Chance to keep mana sources for a spell predicted for the second main phase (ComputerUtilMana). The closest heuristic-AI knob to not tapping out early.
Default never casts a flash creature in response to a spell; the Azorius and Dimir lists play flash threats.

params.name: kill-evasive
params.why: Whether removal goes first to creatures that cannot be blocked (flyers), always or only when life is in danger, instead of the biggest threat.

params.name: protect-planeswalkers
params.why: Several reactive lists win with planeswalkers; Default only chump-blocks for one when the attack would kill it.
Lets the AI pay sacrifice costs with cheap creatures and tokens when a card has no sacrifice preference of its own (Jund Sacrifice; Reckless enables it).
Hand size below which the AI stops mulliganing (Default 4). Slow decks suffer more from going to four or five.
Despite the name this acts with Monte Carlo off: the deck-plan mulligan (simulation.OpeningHand) instead of the old land-count rule. On by default (the AiProps default; Default.ai does not set it).
The archetype the deck-plan mulligan judges hands by; 'auto' (default) reads it from the list and may call a value deck aggro.
As above, for the creature decks.
